title: A strong defense industry may be Ukraine's best security guarantee
gist: Ahead of renewed Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, the piece (raw byline Peter Dickinson; text's bio credits Leonid Baratz) argues that with NATO membership off the table, the Coalition of the Willing constrained, and written guarantees discredited by the Budapest Memorandum, Ukraine's best security guarantee is its own defense industry, which has grown from ~$1B to a projected $55B in 2026 output. It urges Kyiv to cut export fees and fast-track licenses, and Europe to buy Ukrainian systems for its own armies.
